The #GoogleDoodle is celebrating World Space Week 🚀 Head into low Earth orbit to explore life above Earth, powered by human curiosity, ingenuity, and innovation. Swipe through the incredible views, one question at a time.

what is the overview effect and why does seeing earth from space change astronauts forever|

The overview effect is a cognitive shift in awareness and perspective experienced by astronauts when viewing Earth from space, characterized by an overwhelming sense of awe, a deep realization of human interconnectedness, and a stark awareness of the planet's fragility. 

Explore more with Google Search

can astronauts in orbit tell which country they're flying over|

Yes, astronauts always know which country they are flying over because they use onboard digital maps and GPS systems.

what is it like to live and float in space|

Living and floating in space is a surreal, physically transformative experience defined by microgravity, where traditional rules of up and down completely disappear.

what is the most anticipated food delivery on the international space station|

Fresh produce – specifically fruits and vegetables like apples, oranges, tomatoes, and onions – is the single most anticipated food delivery aboard the International Space Station.

how many people can live aboard the space station at the same time|

The International Space Station typically hosts a standard crew of 7 but has briefly reached a maximum of 13 people aboard.

is the great wall of china really visible from space with the naked eye|

No, the Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye under normal conditions. From low Earth orbit, human eyes cannot spot an object that thin and low contrast without help.

how many people have actually been to the international space station|

Over 290 people have visited the International Space Station since it first welcomed a human crew in November 2000.

how long does it take to send an email from space before it's received, is there a lag|

Warning: These slides may cause existential wonder ✨To celebrate World Space Week, today’s #GoogleDoodle spotlights a never-before-seen photo of the Rosebud Nebula – a cosmic stellar nursery located 3,300 light-years away, captured by the James Webb Telescope.  

Keep swiping for distant planets and cosmic phenomena, along with answers to a few of the millions of questions they spark  🌌

what is cosmic dust and how is it so thick|

Cosmic dust is a collection of tiny solid particles – microscopic grains of carbon, silicates, and ice – that float through outer space. Although they appear remarkably thick and solid, their apparent density is an illusion caused by immense scale.

Explore more with Google Search

why is jupiter’s north pole glowing electric blue|
 
Jupiter’s north pole glows electric blue because of a gigantic, permanent ultraviolet aurora caused by high-energy particles, gas excitation, and volcanic power.

what are the clouds in the carina nebula made of|

The clouds in the Carina Nebula are made of molecular gas and cosmic dust, with the main components being hydrogen, smaller amounts of ionized elements like oxygen, sulfur, and nitrogen – which give the nebula its colorful glow – and tiny grains of heavier elements like carbon and silicates.

how far away is our closest giant galactic neighbor, andromeda, and is it true it’s heading toward us| 

The Andromeda Galaxy is about 2.5 million light-years away from us, and it is indeed heading straight toward the Milky Way. Traveling at roughly 68 to 110 miles per second (110–180 km/s), the galaxies will collide and merge in about 4 to 4.5 billion years.

what are the massive bubbles that appear in space|

Massive bubbles in space are giant cavities or shells of hot, superthin gas carved out by exploding stars, stellar winds, or outbursts from supermassive black holes.

how can an ancient star cluster be made of “heavy metal”|

We’re bringing new voice capabilities to @GoogleWorkspace to help you tackle daily tasks. Swipe ➡️ to learn how Gmail, Google Docs, and Keep can help you search your inbox, organize your thoughts, and brainstorm new ideas conversationally.

Conversational search can help you find quick answers to questions like, "What’s my flight's gate number?" or "What’s going on at my kid’s school this week?"

Just talk as if you’re speaking to a friend, and Docs Live handles the heavy lifting: organizing your thoughts, structuring your document, and — with your permission — pulling relevant details directly from your Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the broader web.

Keep is usually used to note a quick idea or something that crosses your mind before you forget it. Now, you can talk to Keep Live to capture, structure, and refine your ideas into organized, actionable notes.

Head to the link in bio to learn more.
